live_qualified_tools.name: arrange_pages
live_qualified_tools.description: Reorder the page list and add or remove dividers in one call. Dividers are visual separators between groups of pages. Pass the complete new order; the call is rejected without changes if it misses an item or lists an unknown or repeated ID, which also happens when pages were added or removed since you read the list. Pages are never deleted. Does not switch which page the user is viewing. Returns the resulting page list, including the IDs of new dividers.

order.description: The complete page list in its new order: every page and divider ID from get_basic_info exactly once, except dividers listed in removeDividerIds. Put { "type": "divider" } where a new divider should go.

removeDividerIds.description: IDs of existing dividers to remove.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

live_qualified_tools.name: create_file
live_qualified_tools.description: Create a new Paper file in the user's active team and returns the new file's ID, name, parentId, and URL. Pass parentId to create it inside a folder; otherwise it is created in the active team's top-level folder. To start working in the new file, call open_file with the returned ID.

cloneFileId.description: Optional file ID to clone from. If provided, the new file is a copy of this one.

name.description: Optional display name for the new file.

parentId.description: Optional ID of the folder to create the new file in. Defaults to the active team's top-level folder. Use list_resources to find folder IDs.

live_qualified_tools.name: create_page
live_qualified_tools.description: Creates a new page in the file and returns its ID. The page is added after the page the user is viewing; use arrange_pages to move it. To work on the new page use the returned pageId in subsequent tool calls.

name.description: Optional display name for the new page (shown in the page list). Defaults to "Page N".

icon.description: Icon shown in place of the default page icon in the page list. Icons are decorative and do not change page behavior. About some icons: arrow: Depicts a thick arrow pointing to the right. May be used to indicate the key page in a file, as it points towards the page name in the page list, helping it stand out from other pages. design: Depicts a pencil crossed over a ruler. paper: Depicts a piece of crumpled paper. May be used to indicate previous drafts or discarded work that is no longer relevant.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

live_qualified_tools.name: get_basic_info
live_qualified_tools.description:
Get essential context about the current design: file name, page name, node count, artboards with their dimensions, font families used, a compact list of design tokens.
Call get_basic_info first to understand the canvas situation.
- When no fileId is provided the file the user is viewing is used.
- Pass pageId to inspect a specific page; omit to use the page the user is viewing.
- worldX/worldY properties are the world position of the node
- worldX/worldY/width/height are null when the size or position depends on layout (e.g. fit-content, flex children) and the node was not measured (i.e. the page is inactive)
- pages lists the page list in display order: pages (type "page") and dividers (type "divider"), which separate groups of pages and have no canvas, so their IDs cannot be used as pageId
- the page with isActive is what the user sees and controls, and it can change while you work if the user switches pages
- you can work on other pages without disrupting the user by passing their pageId to page-scoped tools (create_artboard, export, get_basic_info); tools that take a nodeId act on whichever page the node lives on

pageId.description: The page ID that the tool should operate on. When omitted the active page will be used. The active page can change between tool calls, prefer passing explicit page IDs.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on. When omitted the file the user is viewing is used.

live_qualified_tools.name: list_resources
live_qualified_tools.description: Lists files and folders. Each item has type "file" or "folder" and parentId, omitted for a top-level folder and for an open file that is not in the active team’s resources. Open files are listed first. `open` means the file is a desktop tab. `active` means that tab is in the foreground. Both apply only to files. `draft` means the item is in the user’s drafts. Then files and folders recently updated in the active team. Timestamps are omitted when an open file is not in the active team’s resources. Pass parentId to list only what is inside one folder. Pass a higher limit until truncated is absent before treating the list as the whole tree.

limit.description: Maximum number of files and folders to return. Defaults to 50. Sorted by updatedAt, most recent first.

includeArchived.description: Optional. Also list archived files and folders, marked archived. Use to find IDs for unarchive_resources.

parentId.description: Optional folder ID. Only list the files and folders directly inside this folder.

live_qualified_tools.name: move_nodes
live_qualified_tools.description:
Move one or more existing nodes. Preserves node identity (IDs stay the same), so any references you are holding continue to work. Prefer this over duplicate+delete or rewriting HTML when you just want to reposition or reparent existing layers.

Each move uses one of two shapes:
1. Sibling-relative: { nodeId, before: siblingId } or { nodeId, after: siblingId }. The destination parent is inferred from the sibling.
2. Parent-absolute: { nodeId, parentId, index? }. The node is placed at the given index under parentId, or appended if index is omitted. index is clamped to [0, childCount] — use 0 for first. Pass parentId: 'root' as a shortcut for the page root of the page the node currently lives on.

Use shape sibling-relative shape 1 when you already know a neighbor; use parent-absolute shape 2 when you want to move into a specific parent (or to the end of one).

Notes:
- Moves apply sequentially; later moves in the same batch see earlier changes.
- For flex/flow parents this changes visual order. For freeform parents this changes stacking (last child renders on top) and does not move the node's world position.
- When moving to a new parent, Paper may adjust layout-related styles (width/height intents like filling available space) may be adjusted so the node does not collapse to zero size in the new parent.
- You can move nodes between pages
- Cannot move the root. Cannot target a node that cannot have children. Cannot move a node under itself or any of its own descendants. For before/after, the sibling cannot be the moved node itself.
Returns resolved parentId and index for each successful move, plus affectedParents — the post-batch children list of every parent whose order changed (both sources and destinations, deduplicated). Use affectedParents to refresh your mental model of the tree without a follow-up get_children.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node to move.

before.description: Place the node immediately before this sibling. The target parent is inferred from the sibling.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node to move.

after.description: Place the node immediately after this sibling. The target parent is inferred from the sibling.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node to move.

parentId.description: The ID of the destination parent. Must be able to have children (e.g. Frames). Pass the string `'root'` as a shortcut for the page root of the page the node currently lives on (same as that page's rootNodeId from get_basic_info).

index.description: The final index among the destination parent's children. Clamped to [0, childCount]. Use 0 for first, or omit to append at the end.

moves.description: Move operations, applied sequentially. Each operation sees the updated tree from prior operations.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

live_qualified_tools.name: rename_resource
live_qualified_tools.description: Rename a file or folder. Sets the display name shown in the file browser. Pass the file or folder ID. The stored name is trimmed and capped at 500 characters. An empty name leaves the current name unchanged. Returns the stored name and whether the resource is a file or a folder.

resourceId.description: The ID of the file or folder to rename.

name.description: The new display name for the file or folder.

live_qualified_tools.name: update_pages
live_qualified_tools.description: Change the name and/or icon of one or more pages in the file. Does not switch which page the user is viewing. Supports batch updates in a single call.

pageId.description: The ID of the page to update. Use get_basic_info to list pages.

name.description: The new display name for the page (shown in the page list). Omit to leave it unchanged.

icon.description: Icon shown in place of the default page icon in the page list. Icons are decorative and do not change page behavior. About some icons: arrow: Depicts a thick arrow pointing to the right. May be used to indicate the key page in a file, as it points towards the page name in the page list, helping it stand out from other pages. design: Depicts a pencil crossed over a ruler. paper: Depicts a piece of crumpled paper. May be used to indicate previous drafts or discarded work that is no longer relevant. Omit to leave it unchanged, or pass null to restore the default page icon.

updates.description: Array of page updates. Each item specifies a page ID and the fields to change.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

blocked_upstream_schema_provenance: Matching protected tests/fixtures/paper_desktop/16e6b_full_catalog.json; descriptors are not callable through bridge.

blocked_upstream_tools.name: archive_resources
blocked_upstream_tools.description: Archive files and folders. Archiving a folder also archives everything inside it. Archived items move to the Archive page in the file browser and are only returned by list_resources with includeArchived. Use unarchive_resources to restore them. Every ID is checked first: if any of them cannot be archived, nothing is archived. Team files and the user's drafts are saved separately, so if saving one fails, the error lists the items that were still archived. Returns the archived items.

resourceIds.description: The IDs of the files and folders to archive. Use list_resources to find IDs.

blocked_upstream_tools.name: create_folder
blocked_upstream_tools.description: Create a new folder in the file browser and returns its ID, name, parentId, and URL. Pass parentId to nest it inside another folder; otherwise it is created in the active team's top-level folder. The stored name is trimmed and capped at 500 characters.

name.description: Optional display name for the new folder. Defaults to "Untitled project".

parentId.description: Optional ID of the folder to create the new folder in. Defaults to the active team's top-level folder. Use list_resources to find folder IDs.

blocked_upstream_tools.name: delete_nodes
blocked_upstream_tools.description:
Delete one or more nodes from the design. Also deletes all descendants of the specified nodes.
IMPORTANT: Before deleting nodes that you think have an incorrect parent verify using get_node_info first.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

nodeIds.description: Array of node IDs to delete.

blocked_upstream_tools.name: export
blocked_upstream_tools.description: Export nodes as image or video files. Unless the user specifies, do not override the default export settings. Returns each export's file path, or on Paper's remote MCP server a download link that works for 24 hours. PDF exports require Paper Desktop.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

anyOf.description: Exports all nodes on the target page that already have export settings. Uses pageId when provided, otherwise the page the user is viewing. Ignored when exporting explicit node IDs.

additionalProperties.description: Used to override the default export settings for the node. Set to an empty array `[]` to export with default settings.

durationSeconds.description: Video duration in seconds. Only applicable when type is "video".

format.description: Format to export the node as. SVG exports are only supported for SVG nodes. For video, use "mp4" (opaque, page background) or "webm" (transparent).

pdfQuality.description: PDF image quality for images. Only applicable when format is "pdf".

pdfResampling.description: PDF image resizing resampling strategy. "detailed" preserves fine detail with the Lanczos algorithm, "basic" produces smaller files and uses the Hamming algorithm. Only applicable when format is "pdf".

scale.description: Export scale. A number followed by a unit: "x" (multiplier, e.g. "0.5x", "1x", "2x"), "p" (pixels on shortest side, e.g. "720p", "1440p"), "w" (target width, e.g. "512w"), or "h" (target height, e.g. "512h")

anyOf.description: Record of nodes to export, keyed by nodeId.

pageId.description: The page ID that the tool should operate on. When omitted the active page will be used. The active page can change between tool calls, prefer passing explicit page IDs.

blocked_upstream_tools.name: export_combined_pdf
blocked_upstream_tools.description: Requires Paper Desktop. Export multiple nodes combined into a single PDF file, one page per node. Pages are auto-ordered by canvas position (top-to-bottom, then left-to-right). Use this instead of "export" when the user wants the nodes merged into one PDF rather than separate files. The quality and resampling used is the highest of any existing PDF export settings found on individual nodes.

fileId.description: The file ID that the tool should operate on.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs to combine into a single PDF, one page per node. Pages are auto-ordered by top-to-bottom then left-to-right canvas position.

blocked_upstream_tools.name: move_resources
blocked_upstream_tools.description: Move files and folders into another folder. A folder moves with everything inside it, so pass a folder or items inside it, not both. Items can only move within the same place: team files stay in the team, drafts stay in the user's drafts. Every ID is checked first: if any of them cannot be moved, nothing is moved. Returns the moved items. Items already in the folder are listed separately and left as they are.

parentId.description: The ID of the folder to move them into. Use list_resources to find folder IDs.

resourceIds.description: The IDs of the files and folders to move. Use list_resources to find IDs.

blocked_upstream_tools.name: open_file
blocked_upstream_tools.description: Opens a Paper file by its ID or URL. Optional pageId is applied only on the initial open; if the file is already open the page will not switch. Returns a get_basic_info response.

fileId.description: The Paper file ID to open. Accepts a bare ID, a /file/<id> route path, or the files URL.

pageId.description: Optional page ID to open. Only applied when the file is not already open — if the file is already open the current page is left unchanged so the user is not pulled away from what they are looking at. A page ID in a /file/<id>/<pageId> URL passed as fileId is also accepted.

blocked_upstream_tools.name: unarchive_resources
blocked_upstream_tools.description: Unarchive files and folders. Unarchiving a folder also unarchives everything inside it. An item whose folder is still archived is moved to the top-level folder, unless that folder is also being unarchived. Every ID is checked first: if any of them cannot be unarchived, nothing is unarchived. Team files and the user's drafts are saved separately, so if saving one fails, the error lists the items that were still unarchived. Returns the unarchived items with the parentId each one ended up in.

resourceIds.description: The IDs of the archived files and folders to unarchive. Use list_resources with includeArchived to find IDs.

create_file.required: name plus exactly one existing cloneFileId or bridge-only sourceFileId
create_file.publication: HOLD: current client action prohibits file creation

rename_resource.resourceType: exact existing FILE only, not folder

bridge_constraints.name: Applies only to file management (create_file / rename_resource): nonblank after trimming, with trimmed length 1..500. Callers should send trimmed names; bridge forwards the supplied string. No undocumented create_file normalization is asserted.
bridge_constraints.arrange_pages: complete current page/divider IDs once, except removed dividers; no page deletion
bridge_constraints.all_mutations: own current permission, target scope, snapshot and operation ID required; catalog compatibility is not admission
